proposed_comments.title: Handle selection shortcuts after Alt is released
proposed_comments.body: ### Handle selection shortcuts after Alt is released`n`n**Severity:** `high``n`n**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/QuickAccessShelfShortcuts.cs` (`IsSelectionShortcut` and `ResolveSelectionShortcut`).`n`n**Suggested change:** Treat `AccessKeyManager.IsDisplayModeEnabled` as an alternate entry condition for the Shift+number selection chord, not only the current `alt` modifier. Windows can report the shortcut after Alt has been released while key-tip display mode remains active; pass that state through both helpers and preserve the existing Ctrl/Shift/Win and visible-count checks. Add a regression test for `alt: false` while key-tip display mode is enabled.

confidence.rationale: The current upstream helper requires alt to be true, while the validated candidate adds the key-tip display-mode condition and a matching regression test.

proposed_comments.title: Resolve key-tip selection before requiring a focused shelf button
proposed_comments.body: ### Resolve key-tip selection before requiring a focused shelf button`n`n**Severity:** `high``n`n**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs` (`TryHandleQuickAccessShelfItemKeyDown`).`n`n**Suggested change:** Evaluate `ResolveSelectionShortcut` immediately after confirming the shelf is visible, pass `AccessKeyManager.IsDisplayModeEnabled`, and consume visible or unavailable selection chords before calling `FindQuickAccessShelfButton`. In key-tip display mode the original source can be a non-button element, so the current early anchor lookup can prevent the numbered shelf selection from being recognized. Keep the existing Enter/context-command handling behind the anchor lookup, and preserve the native access-key focus behavior for a visible target.

confidence.rationale: The current upstream hunk performs the anchor lookup before selection resolution; the validated candidate moves resolution first, passes key-tip mode, and consumes the visible target path.

proposed_comments.title: Add regression coverage for released-Alt key-tip selection
proposed_comments.body: ### Add regression coverage for released-Alt key-tip selection`n`n**Severity:** `medium``n`n**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/QuickAccessShelfResolverTests.cs` (`QuickAccessShelfResolverTests`).`n`n**Suggested change:** Extend the new shortcut tests with a case where `alt` is false, Shift is true, the numbered key is within the visible range, and key-tip display mode is true; assert that `IsSelectionShortcut` and `ResolveSelectionShortcut` accept it as a visible target. This locks the Windows key-tip transition behavior and prevents a future refactor from restoring the Alt-only condition.

confidence.rationale: The current upstream test hunk lacks coverage for the released-Alt transition; the validated candidate adds both the predicate assertion and visible-target resolver test.
